implementation: launchMigrationProcessTree accepts only an explicit runner, existing absolute executable/cwd, a bounded operationId and 0-64 bounded argv strings. It canonicalizes paths, rejects symlinks and wrong file types, never uses PATH or a shell, and is private owner-only component code.

The existing native ProcessJob.cs runner is spawned directly and receives one bounded JSON request. The native CreateProcess Job-list admission, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and creator watchdog are reused without modifying frozen DS/SDK code or the C# source.

Only native runner close produces treeStopped:true with stopEvidence:'windows-job-close'. stop() targets exactly the owned wrapper, waits bounded for the original close result and is idempotent. Timeout answers MIGRATION_OS_QUARANTINE_STOP_UNKNOWN.

Every result and snapshot carries externalRestartBlocked:false, persistentExternalExclusion:false and stopWriteProvable:false. There is no release or activate method and cancellation is not represented as rollback.

Synchronous spawn failures such as Windows EFTYPE are normalized to MIGRATION_OS_QUARANTINE_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE; asynchronous runner-start failure is consumed and reports runnerNotStarted:true and treeStopped:false rather than a fabricated Job stop receipt.

limitations: W06.15 remains in_progress. Dedicated-account and device validation, persistent external restart exclusion, real old entry points, write-handle closure across all domains, Linux, full migration activation and production acceptance remain open.
A Windows Job is process-tree containment, not an account, AppContainer, filesystem or storage fencing boundary. It cannot constrain a process outside the controlled launch tree.
The adapter requires a trusted prebuilt runner; tests compile the repository ProcessJob.cs into an isolated tmp directory. The component does not compile or install a runner in production.
